Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard Sri Lal Prabhakar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State, Sri Rajendra Prasad, learned counsel appearing for the opposite party No. 2 and perused the record.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant with a prayer to quash the order dated 04.01.2023 whereby application under Section 320(2) Cr.P.C. of the applicant has been rejected and further proceedings of Session Trial No. 2439 of 2022 (State Vs. Rakesh and others),
arising out of Case Crime No. 54 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Kurh Fatehgarh, District Sambhal, pending in the court of learned Civil Judge (J.D.), Chandausi.

sentences.text: 1 It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is wife of opposite party No. 2.

Their marriage was solemnized in the year 2004, but on account of acrimonious relation at that time, the applicant lodged the impugned F.I.R. on 28.05.2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, making allegation of harassment etc. against opposite party No. 2 and his family members.
Investigation Officer after investigation submitted charge-sheet on 04.10.2022.

Thereafter, the parties concerned entered into a compromise outside the Court,
original copy of said compromise deed is annexed as Annexure No. 1 to the supplementary affidavit dated15.07.2024.

After making compromise, applicant moved an application dated 04.01.2023 under Section 320(2) Cr.P.C. to drop the further proceedings against the accused on the ground of compromise, which has been wrongly and illegally rejected by the trial court vide impugned order dated 04.01.2023.
It is also submitted that as on date applicant is living with her husband/opposite party No. 2 along with her daughter and leading her marital life happily.

On the strength of aforesaid facts it is submitted that on account of compromise arrived at between the parties concerned, all disputes between them have come to an end, therefore, aforesaid criminal proceeding against the applicant is liable to be quashed by this Court.
Learned Additional Government Advocate for the State as well as learned counsel appearing on behalf of opposite party no. 2 do not dispute the aforesaid facts.

After having heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties, I find that after settlement arrived at between the parties in the present case, the chance of ultimate conviction of opposite party no. 2 is bleak and, therefore, no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution against the opposite party no. 2 to continue, as the same would be futile exercise and a sheer wastage of precious time of the Court.
The continuation of a criminal proceedings after compromise would cause oppression and prejudice to the parties concerned.

If the parties concerned wants to bury the hatchet and are willing to move on in a matrimonial dispute on the basis of compromise, they may be allowed to compound the offences in terms of settlement, because in such circumstances the proceedings can hardly be taken to their logical culmination and, the prospect of conviction gets lost.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case in the light of dictum and guidelines laid down by the Apex Court in case of B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another, (2003) 1 SCC (Cri) 848 and State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, AIR 2019 SC 1296, this Court feels that this is a fit case, where this Court can exercise its inherent power to secure the ends of justice.

In view of the above, impugned order dated 04.01.2023 and further proceedings of Session Trial No.
2439 of 2022 (State Vs. Rakesh and others) against the opposite party no. 2 are hereby quashed.
In the conspectus of the aforesaid, this application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed in terms of compromise as mentioned above.
